title: Enterprise Reserved GPU — Intake Scoring & Scaling Playbook
creator: Priya Nair
description: Goal: Produce a repeatable intake and prioritization playbook for enterprise reserved GPU requests that maps customer SLA targets and workload characteristics to recommended reserved throughput, GPU family profile, and scaling policy. Background: We continue to see large enterprise requests that require guaranteed throughput and latency SLAs but vary wildly in model choice, token distributions, and burst behavior. Current triage relies on ad-hoc PM/solutions judgment and engineering capacity conversations. This playbook creates a scoring rubric, a decision matrix for GPU family selection (A100v5, H100, L4, T4-like inference), and fallback/runbook guidance (burst policies, preemption, regional fallback) to reduce intake-to-commit cycle time and improve predictability for sales/solutions teams. Scope: - Enterprise reserved pools (monthly/annual commitments) only. Excludes on-demand hosted API and one-off POCs. - Covers SLA definitions (p99 latency, throughput QPS, steady-state tokens/sec), recommended reserved throughput sizing, GPU family recommendation, scaling policy template (autoscale trigger thresholds, burst window, preemptible fallback). Deliverables: - Scoring rubric PDF and one-page decision matrix. - Intake form updates for Sales/Customer Success. - Engineering runbook with autoscale parameter presets and required telemetry. - Example sizing for three canonical customer archetypes.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Scoring rubric documented and validated with Solutions Engineering and two enterprise customers
A2: Decision matrix maps requested SLA and workload signal to a recommended reserved throughput and GPU family with <= 1 week engineering review
A3: Intake form in Zendesk/CRM updated and linked to the playbook
A4: Engineering accepts three autoscale presets (latency-sensitive, throughput-first, cost-constrained) and provides implementation PR
A5: Sales has a one-page quick reference and a signed internal alignment doc for offer windows and burst policy

notes: Scoring rubric sketch: Score = 0.35*latency_urgency + 0.25*steady_throughput + 0.15*burst_ratio + 0.15*model_complexity + 0.10*business_priority. Latency_urgency maps p99 target bands to 0..10. Model_complexity derived from tokenizer length, decoder steps, and known perf profile. Overrides: data_residency_flag => require Private deployment review; regulatory must be escalated to Solutions Eng and Security for contract addendum. Example outcome: Customer A (chat p99 120ms, steady 50 QPS, peak 300 QPS, model Llama-4-XS) => score 7.8 => recommended reserved throughput 100 QPS on L4-class GPUs with burst window 5 minutes and preemption fallback to hosted API in region. Example outcome: Customer B (batch embeddings p99 2000ms ok, steady 500 QPS, peak 1200 QPS, model open-embed-16k) => score 6.2 => recommend H100 reserved pool with throughput reservation 600 QPS and aggressive batching config.
